issue_context.title: `journalctl --follow --cursor-file` does not update cursor
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252.5-2~bpo11+1

### Used distribution

Debian 11

### Linux kernel version used

5.10.0-20-amd64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

journalctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

`journalctl --follow --cursor-file` should update the cursor file, at least when it exits normally. (I will leave it up to the developers what "normally" means here, but there should be *some* way to terminate journalctl so that it updates the cursor file.)

Ideally, `journalctl --follow --cursor-file` should just regularly update the cursor file while it is running, like `systemd-journal-upload --save-state` does.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

I could not find any way to meaningfully use `journalctl --follow` with a cursor. Neither `--cursor-file` nor `--show-cursor` write/print a new cursor.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Run `journalctl --follow --cursor-file=some-cursor-file`
2. Write something new to the journal
3. Terminate journalctl through Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, etc.
4. Observe that the cursor-file has not changed

review_comments:
> One minor(?) behavior change is that 'journalctl --follow' now exits with 0 on terminate e.g. with ctrl-C.

That's actually a regression. I'm not sure if anyone relies on this, but previously we were returning correct information but now we're suppressing it.

E.g. when I run this silly example in fish, the result looks strange:
```console
[0] $ tail -f /etc/fstab | build/journalctl -f | grep foobar
^C⏎
[SIGINT|0|SIGINT] $
```
